sentiment: We made it fast and stopped looking. The crack in the old paint program proves someone finally did.

stories.title: MS Paint Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
stories.summary: Thirty years of muscle memory, and the paint program turns out to have been a door the whole time. Nobody audited it because nobody thought of it as software — it was just the thing you opened to waste an afternoon. The oldest tool in the room is the one we stopped reading.

stories.title: sshole
stories.summary: A small utility with a rude name, built to do one narrow thing well, and the internet hands it the top of the page for a day. There is no marketing in it. Someone got tired of a small friction and removed it, which is still the most reliable way anything good gets made.

stories.title: Blender's UI and Runtime: Much Faster Than GPUI
stories.summary: The interesting claim is not the benchmark, it is the archaeology: the speed was already there, buried in decisions made years ago by people who are not in the room. We keep rediscovering that the fast version of a thing is usually the one that was built carefully first.
